clause_evidence.reasoning: The packet contains contextual questions requiring learners to determine elapsed times, month intervals, and weekdays rather than only naming isolated facts.
The rendered set uses clocks, calendars, and a timetable to ask concrete questions about time and elapsed duration.
Several samples explicitly ask for or calculate whole-hour endpoints and durations, including 8:00 to 9:00 and 9:00 to 12:00.
Multiple items explicitly state 30 minutes or show a half-hour interval and require the learner to determine the endpoint or duration.
Quarter-hour understanding is present in the 15-minute break and reading-time items, but it receives much less representation than whole- and half-hour cases.
The packet asks which weekday a date falls on, but no printed sample asks learners to determine or use the fact that a week has seven days.
Month names and month-to-month intervals appear often, but no sample directly establishes or uses the complete count of twelve months in a year.
